conventions.convention: S is finite. Diagram edges occur exactly when m(s,t) ≥ 3; label 3 is omitted and m(s,t)=2 draws no edge. Finite type means W finite. The empty system is not irreducible.
B(e_s,e_s)=1; off-diagonal entries are −cos(π/m(s,t)), with coefficient −1 for m=∞. No definiteness or nondegeneracy is assumed initially.
Component products and direct sums include empty rank: the empty group product is trivial, the empty vector-space sum is zero, and positive definiteness is vacuous on zero space.
Scaled Cartan entries are a_st=B(a_s,a_t∨), with rows indexed by roots and columns by coroots. The published row-coroot Cartan matrix is Aᵀ.
A lattice is a discrete subgroup spanning V. Q and Q∨ are lattices; P is a lattice exactly when B is nondegenerate. With degenerate B, the name weight lattice makes no discreteness assertion.
W^J tests right ascents and represents left cosets wW_J; the dual-functional orbit uses these same cosets. Schreier edges use left multiplication by generators.

P_A is a coefficientwise formal series over Z, with finite length fibers; it is a unit exactly when 1 ∈ A. Descent intervals are inclusive: I ⊆ D_R(w) ⊆ J. The marked multivariate descent polynomial requires finite W.
The Steinberg sum here runs over all subsets K ⊆ S, using formal inverses: its value is t^ℓ(w₀)/P_W for finite W and zero for infinite W. Substitution t↦t⁻¹ is interpreted in Q(t), not in Z[[t]].
Classical diagram ranks and permutation sizes differ: A_n corresponds to S_(n+1). D₂=A₁×A₁ and D₃=A₃ are separate recurrence bases; the D_n degree multiset repeats degree n when n is even.
AC is assumed for basic-degree determination and the degree comparison. The orbit-distance certificates, classical growth calculations and longest-element reciprocity argument use no further choice.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite set S with Coxeter matrix m, presented group W and canonical Coxeter form B: W is finite if and only if B is positive definite. When B is positive definite, b(v)=B(v,·) is an equivariant linear isomorphism V→V*. Both canonical images are discrete, without a positivity assumption for that discreteness clause.

For connected Γ, W is finite exactly when Γ is A_n (n≥1), B_n (n≥2), D_n (n≥4), E₆,E₇,E₈,F₄,H₃,H₄ or I₂(m) (3≤m<∞). For arbitrary finite S, finiteness holds exactly when every component is listed; W is then the product of its component parabolics. The listed diagrams are positive definite, with the stated doubled-determinant table and low-rank coincidences.

For diagram components S_i, multiplication gives an isomorphism ∏W_(S_i)→W with additive length, and V is the B-orthogonal sum of the component spaces. Every ρ(W)-invariant symmetric bilinear form is a scalar multiple of B on each component. A positive-definite invariant form forces B positive definite; finite W supplies such a form by averaging.

A connected positive-definite Coxeter diagram is acyclic, satisfies Σ_(t∈N(s))c(s,t)²<1, has at most one branch vertex and at most one label ≥4, and a large label excludes branching. Path determinants satisfy d₀=d₁=1 and d_k=d_(k−1)−cos²(π/m_(k−1))d_(k−2). A single large edge with split sizes i≤j requires (i+1)(j+1)>4ij cos²(π/m); an all-3 three-arm star requires 1/(p+1)+1/(q+1)+1/(r+1)>1.

For a scaling, a_st a_ts=4cos²(π/m(s,t)), with product 4 for m=∞. Positive-definite crystallographic scalings have labels 2,3,4,6. Forests with edge labels 3,4,6 admit the stated positive tree scaling. Every crystallographic scaling has reflection-stable Q and Q∨, Q=ZΦ_c, Q∨=ZΦ_c∨, Q⊆P, integral root-coroot pairings and one-sign integral root coordinates.

Assume W finite. A crystallographic scaling exists exactly when every edge label lies in {3,4,6}, equivalently every component is A,B,D,E,F or G₂. Its scaled root set is a reduced crystallographic Euclidean root system with base {a_s}, Weyl group ρ(W), and the stated lattice stability. No other finite Coxeter system is a Weyl system with standard generators corresponding to a base. Reversing the unique multiple-edge length ratio transposes the scaled Cartan matrix.

For finite S, every descent parabolic is finite; finite W_J has D_L(w₀(J))=D_R(w₀(J))=J. Parabolic multiplication is length-additive and bijective, giving P_W=P_(W^J)P_(W_J)=P_(^JW)P_(W_J). For I⊆J⊆S, D_I^J=Σ_(J\I⊆K⊆J)(−1)^|J\K|P_(W^(S\K)). The all-subsets Steinberg sum is t^ℓ(w₀)/P_W for finite W and zero for infinite W. Every finite-rank Coxeter growth series is rational.

Fix s₀∈S, T=S\{s₀}, and f₀(e_s)=δ_(s,s₀). Then Stab_W(f₀)=W_T and W/W_T→W·f₀ is an equivariant bijection. The minimum length of an element carrying f₀ to v equals the Schreier graph distance d(v), with |d(sv)−d(v)|≤1, and P_W=P_(W_T)Σ_v t^d(v). W_T need not be finite.

The specified canonical representations identify with permutation, signed-permutation, even-signed-permutation and dihedral models. Their selected parabolic orbit quotients give P_(A_n)=[n+1]_t!, P_(B_n)=∏_(i=1)^n[2i]_t, P_(D_n)=[n]_t∏_(i=1)^(n−1)[2i]_t and P_(I₂(m))=[2]_t[m]_t, with the stated low-rank bases and rank ranges. No invariant degrees or choice enter this item.

Under AC for the basic-degree comparison, the exact certificates for E₆,E₇,E₈,F₄,H₃,H₄ describe closed dual-functional orbits with attaining words and an edge-distance bound. Their sizes are 27,56,240,24,12,120. The resulting quotient polynomials, combined with D₅,E₆,E₇,B₃,I₂(5),H₃ parabolic products respectively, give P_W=∏_(d∈D(W))[d]_t for all six types.

Assume AC for degree determination. For every finite Coxeter system, including empty rank and reducible systems, P_W(t)=∏_i[d_i]_t=∏_i(1+t+⋯+t^e_i), with P_W(1)=|W|=∏_i d_i. For N=|Φ_+|=ℓ(w₀)=Σ_i e_i, t^N P_W(t⁻¹)=P_W(t); the reciprocity proof uses the longest-element bijection independently of the product.

concerns.concern: The final prerequisite paragraph quotes the collision theorem as “w·f=g⇒f=g, w∈W_{S(f)}” without stating f,g∈C. The opened supplier thm-cg-dual-chamber-intersections-and-point-stabilizers (3) requires both points in C. Without that restriction the displayed implication is false: take f∈C° and g=s·f. The owned finiteness theorem's F7 retains the correct hypotheses; this concerns the abbreviated page quotation.

Statement (3) says “the exponent comparison Σ_i e_i=N is not used to determine the degrees.” The cited thm-cg-regular-coxeter-eigenvectors-determine-basic-degrees, Proof 3.1, explicitly uses Σ_i e_i=|Φ_+|=nh/2 from its Jacobian supplier to eliminate multiples of h and determine the degrees. The intended independence from the growth-based comparison is sound, but this sentence should distinguish that comparison from the independently proved Jacobian sum.

seams_checked.note: Item-level F7 faithfully quotes collision and stabilizers for f,g∈C. The page's final abbreviated collision formula omits f,g∈C; recorded as a presentation concern.
Growth F4 and product F5 retain finite-W or finite-W_J hypotheses and quote the longest-element involution and length-complement identities accurately.
Descent definitions and quotient sides agree: W^J represents wW_J, with right ascents and additive factorization w=dv. The orbit lemma uses these same left cosets.

Degree-table quotations preserve AC, multiplicities including even D_n, noncrystallographic types, and component unions. The separate wording concern concerns how independence is described, not the quoted degree tables.
Growth F3 quotes full descent inside W_J forcing finiteness and the longest element. Proof 1.1 first factors the ambient element into W_J, meeting that hypothesis.
Arrangement definition and tiling F1 assume finite W before asserting positive-definite B and using b:V→V*. No identification through a degenerate form is imported.
Complexification F4, spectrum F3, component F7 and coincidence quotations preserve finite type, diagram ranks, H/dihedral inclusion and the factorwise orthogonal action.
Nerve Definition (1) and corollary F3 apply W_T finite iff C_T positive definite to the restricted Coxeter system; the empty subset is handled explicitly.
Point-stabilizer F8 quotes the positive-definite crystallographic label restriction. Proof 2.4 constructs precisely that rank-two scaling from inward root normals before applying it.

Proper-parabolic finiteness uses positive-definite principal forms. Enumeration F23 explicitly distinguishes the strict positive-definite path inequality from the ambient semidefinite setting; classification and coincidence quotations retain their hypotheses.
